subject: Recap: Catalog integration discovery — next steps?
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@asterlabs.com>, Priya Singh <priya@asterlabs.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-20T15:08:00-07:00
Subject: Catalog integration discovery — recap & next steps

Hi Jordan and Priya,

Thanks again for taking the time today — great conversation on how Aster's catalog could use an embeddings-backed search layer for product metadata and cross-references. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment: 

What we heard (summary)
- Primary goal: improve discovery for internal teams and partners (reduce time-to-find by surfacing related SKUs).
- Data: product metadata + taxonomy + historical view counts (no PII).
- Priority: pilot to prove relevance lift before Q2 planning.

Open questions we listed
1) Which data source is easiest for a first-pass export (Warehouse export vs S3 dump)?
2) Success metric: do you want click-through improvement or manual relevance score?
3) Security: requirement for dedicated hosting vs hosted API?

Recommended next steps
- Redwood to deliver a 4-week pilot scope and estimate (MVP: ingest ~100k SKUs, embeddings, similarity API, small UI demo).
- Proposed owners: Naomi (Redwood AE) + Aditya (Redwood solutions engineer) for technical onboarding.
- Requested: a sandbox data sample and a 30–45 minute technical deep-dive with engineering.

Proposed timeline
- Sample data shared by: Oct 27
- Technical deep-dive: week of Nov 1
- Pilot start (conditional on access + PO): mid-November

Attachments: proposal + a simple data-flow diagram to illustrate the MVP (see attached).

If this matches your understanding, can you confirm the priority internally and share the best contact on the engineering side (name + email) for the deep-dive? If not, tell me what I missed and I’ll adjust.

Thanks — looking forward to moving this forward if it’s still a priority.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood-catalog-integration-proposal.pdf (PDF, 420KB)]
[Attachment: MVP-data-flow.png (PNG, 95KB)]

From: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@asterlabs.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Singh <priya@asterlabs.com>
Date: 2026-10-22T11:34:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Catalog integration discovery — recap & next steps

Thanks, Naomi — good notes. Quick Qs: 1) Can you provide a ballpark price range for the 4-week pilot and an estimate for running production (hosted vs dedicated)? 2) We have a technical owner, Miguel Alvarez (miguel.alvarez@asterlabs.com) who can join the deep-dive.

Priority: this is on the shortlist for our Q1 roadmap, but we need procurement to sign off on the pilot cost. I’ll loop Miguel and our procurement lead once I have a clearer number.

-Jordan
Director of Product, Aster Labs

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@asterlabs.com>, Priya Singh <priya@asterlabs.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-28T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Catalog integration discovery — recap & next steps

Jordan — great, thanks for the quick reply and for sharing Miguel. 

Ballpark (pilot): $18k–$28k for the 4-week scope (ingest, embeddings, similarity API, and demo UI).
Production ranges a lot depending on throughput and whether you choose hosted API or Redwood Dedicated; typical ranges for similar customers are $5k–$15k/month on hosted, and $20k+/month for a small dedicated pool that gives predictable latency and isolation. We’ll draft a tailored estimate after we see the sample.

Aditya can run the deep-dive — suggested times: Nov 2 (10–11am PT) or Nov 4 (2–3pm PT). Miguel, Priya — does either work?

I attached a one-pager with the pilot line items and a simple pricing cadence so procurement has something to review.

If I don’t hear back on availability, I’ll follow up next week.

Cheers,
Naomi
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: pilot-onepager.pdf (PDF, 120KB)]

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@asterlabs.com>, Priya Singh <priya@asterlabs.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-05T08:54:00-08:00
Subject: Quick pulse — still prioritizing catalog integration?

Hi Jordan / Priya,

Wanted to bump this thread — haven’t seen scheduling or sample data arrive yet. Totally understand procurement cycles, just trying to gauge whether you want us to 1) keep the file active and hold the November deep-dive slots, or 2) pause and re-open later (we can archive the notes and proposal).

Quick options for you to reply with: 
- “Go ahead” — we keep slots open and we’ll hold Nov 2 / Nov 4 windows.
- “Pause” — we’ll archive and check back in 6–8 weeks.
- “Need a different timeline” — tell us when you want us to rebook.

If it helps, we can also provide a lower-cost scoping engagement limited to a data sample ingest and baseline relevance report for ~ $8k.

Thanks — a one-line response is totally fine.

Best,
Naomi
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@asterlabs.com>, Priya Singh <priya@asterlabs.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-18T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Closing the loop — should I close this file?

Jordan / Priya —

Quick note to close the loop on this thread. I haven’t heard back since my last bump (below), so wanted to check where this sits on your list. If this is no longer a near-term priority, we’re happy to close the file and free up our pilot capacity. If you’d like us to keep anything active, pick one of the options below and I’ll act: 

A) "Proceed" — we keep the November slots and Aditya will run the deep-dive. Please share the engineering contact (Miguel) and any sample data before Nov 27.
B) "Lower priority" — please tell us when to check back (e.g., Q1 planning). We'll archive the proposal and set a reminder to re-open.
C) "Archive now" — I’ll mark the opportunity as paused and stop follow-ups; reach out any time and we’ll re-open the thread.

If helpful, here’s the last message I sent on Nov 5 (copied below). No pressure — just trying to keep our pipeline clean so we can prioritize customers actively moving.

Thanks for a quick note either way.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
